service_boundary: Represents the Amazon Bedrock inference platform, not Amazon's model families, SageMaker-hosted endpoints, Amazon Q, or Bedrock AgentCore.
regional_controls: Model, feature, and endpoint availability is region-specific. Inference profiles can route within a geography or globally, while single-region use and provisioned capacity have separate support matrices.
retention_controls: Data handling depends on the selected model, Bedrock feature, region, AWS account controls, and any applicable third-party model terms; cross-region profiles can change the processing locations involved.
routing: Bedrock inference profiles can route a selected model across supported AWS regions; this is regional capacity routing rather than arbitrary cross-model selection.
customization: Eligible base models can be customized, and imported or custom models use distinct identifiers and capacity requirements.
strengths: One AWS control plane covers models from several publishers, regional IAM boundaries, and multiple capacity modes.
Inference profiles and provisioned throughput support production capacity and residency choices.
tradeoffs: Availability and API compatibility vary by model, endpoint, feature, and AWS region.
Third-party models can add publisher-specific terms on top of the AWS agreement.
